samples.summary: The new `setDocument() must not be called inside batch()` guard is not the only path to a whole-document replacement inside a batch — `replaceDocument()` reaches the same state unguarded in both stores, and `setHeader`/`setFooter`'s uninitialized-tree fallback calls `writeFullDocument()` from inside an open batch.
samples.evidence: The guard added at packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:55 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:813 rejects `setDocument()` inside a batch on the stated grounds that a wholesale document load inside a batch would make the loaded document undoable. `MemDocStore.replaceDocument()` (memory.ts:61) does `this.doc = cloneDocument(doc)` with no `batchDepth` check, so a caller inside a batch replaces the document wholesale while the batch's pre-batch checkpoint (memory.ts:206-208) still sits on the undo stack — the exact hazard the guard names, reached without tripping it. Separately, `YorkieDocStore.setHeader`/`setFooter` fall back to `this.writeFullDocument(doc)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:731, 770), and `writeFullDocument` now routes through `withUpdate` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2946), so it executes against the batch's ambient root. The diff's own test at packages/docs/test/model/document.test.ts:1085 calls `store.replaceDocument()` from inside a batch body. Grep shows no production caller of `replaceDocument` today (only the two definitions and tests), so this is a latent bypass of a newly added invariant; impact is undo-history/data integrity, not access control.
searchedFor: grep setDocument in packages/docs/src and packages/frontend/src/app/docs

samples.summary: The batch contract states three prohibitions but only `setDocument` is enforced; `undo()`/`redo()` inside a `MemDocStore` batch silently pops the batch's own checkpoint, with no guard and no test.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/store.ts documents `Do not call undo() / redo() from inside a batch` next to the `setDocument` rule, but only the latter throws. In `MemDocStore`, `batch()` pushes a pre-batch checkpoint (memory.ts:206-208) and `undo()` (memory.ts:157-161) has no `batchDepth` check, so an `undo()` inside a batch pops that checkpoint and reverts the document mid-transaction; the `wroteNothing` reconciliation (memory.ts:230-236) then sees a different stack top and leaves history inconsistent. `YorkieDocStore` is safe only incidentally, because `doc.history.canUndo()` is false while `isUpdating` — an SDK internal the change's own lessons file relies on. Impact is local undo-history corruption / possible loss of in-progress edits, not a security boundary.
searchedFor: reviewed the new batch() describe block in packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts for an undo-inside-batch case
